From: Sam Reynolds <sam.reynolds@hyperpulse.com>

Cc: accounts@hyperpulse.com
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High token count — possible double-count from replay job

Hi Jordan,

We spotted a significant token spike billed to our account across 2026-05-12 00:00–12:00 UTC and believe a background replay job re-processed archived sessions, resulting in ~2.4M extra embed tokens that don't appear in our streaming logs. Attached is a small sample of requests (hyperpulse-token-samples.csv) and the timestamps we expect to be counted only once.

Can Redwood provide a breakdown of the raw request_ids and how those were attributed? We have an outstanding invoice (INV-HP-202605) and need this cleared before our AP team releases payment.

Thanks — we can jump on a short call if that helps.

Sam Reynolds
Head of Platform
HyperPulse Inc.
(attachments: hyperpulse-token-samples.csv)

Hi Sam —

Thanks for flagging this. For our accounting and audit trail well need the following to triage and, if appropriate, apply a retroactive credit:

1) HubSpot deal/contract reference or PO number (you included HP-2024-ENT-42 in your header — please confirm).
2) A short CSV with three columns: request_id, client_timestamp_utc, route (the sample you sent helps but we need full request_ids).
3) Any internal note explaining why the replay ran during the production window — helps us assess intent vs. accidental replays.

Process note: we typically validate disputed tokens against our raw request ledger and internal de-dup logic. If we confirm billing for duplicate ingestion we can offer a credit or invoice adjustment; credits are applied to the next invoice cycle (or as a one-off refund for closed invoices upon mutual agreement).

Ive attached a short guidance doc for preparing the CSV and the preferred log export format (ingest-sample-guidance.txt). Once we receive the file well kick off a token audit and assign a ticket.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: High token count — possible double-count from replay job

Hi Sam — digging into the sample you provided and our trace exports for 2026-05-12. Short summary of what Im seeing:

- Evidence: Several request_ids in your sample (e.g., rq_8f3a2b, rq_8f3a9f) show two ingestion events in our ledger separated by ~5s. The payloads are identical except for a transient prefix tag used by your replay pipeline.
- Likely cause: an offline replay process re-submitted archived sessions without clearing a replay marker; our de-dup heuristics match on full payload hash and request_id but not the prefix tag, so the second ingest was billed.
- Scope estimate: using a sampling approach on the ledger Im seeing ~2.2M tokens that look like duplicates from the same window you flagged.

Proposal for remediation:
1) We prepare a full audit CSV that lists disputed request_ids and the token delta.
2) We propose a provisional credit estimate of 35% of the disputed token charge while we complete a deterministic replay de-dup run. Rationale: sampling shows most duplicates are exact replays, but a minority are legitimate new requests.
3) If the deterministic run confirms full duplication we will apply the remaining credit to zero-out the disputed tokens.

Ive attached a short audit sample (audit-sample-20260512.jsonl) showing how we tag potential duplicates. If youre comfortable with the provisional credit we can move more quickly on invoice IVN-HP-202605.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Principal Systems Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
(attachments: audit-sample-20260512.jsonl)
